html:
The Bangladesh genocide was the mass killing, rape and displacement of Bengalis in East Pakistan by the Pakistan Army and its local allies between March and December 1971.

It began with Operation Searchlight in Dhaka. The army and militias such as the Razakars and Al-Badr then went through towns and villages. They targeted Bengali nationalists, students, intellectuals and the Awami League, and Hindus were attacked as a group. In December, as defeat neared, many writers, doctors and teachers were seized and killed.

The death toll is disputed. Bangladesh says three million. Independent estimates run from about 300,000 to 500,000 or more. Researchers agree that hundreds of thousands of women were raped. About ten million refugees crossed into India, and their care strained its economy and led Indira Gandhi to decide on war.

The killing ended with the Indo-Pakistani War and the birth of Bangladesh. Pakistan has never fully acknowledged the scale. The Blood Telegram shows that US diplomats called it genocide at the time.
sum: The Bangladesh genocide was the mass killing, rape and displacement of Bengalis in East Pakistan by the Pakistan Army and its local allies between March and December 1971.
